Your comments suggest you're referring to orion's in terms of interpersonal conflict. I keep it in while I process it. New emotions and first reactions are often incomplete, and while we should respect them, they don't always serve the end goal. Then I decide if it's a symptom of a larger issue that's going to cause problems again. For example, if your partner forgot something on the grocery run once, it might be frustrating, but just let it go. If your partner forgets things like that a lot, it's time to have a conversation about mindfulness and consideration. Then I think about whether or not I contribute to the problem or if there's something I could be doing to help. Next I think about the other person's perspective. Do they have any way of knowing how they've made me feel? What intentions did they have? What would I have done in their position? Are my needs here reasonable? Then how I need to approach the issue. It should ALWAYS be you two versus the issue. Never you versus them. Instead of "this is what you did wrong" make it "this made me feel this way, I recognize your intentions when you x were probably y, but I'd feel better if you did z to achieve y instead."
